questions.question: The law of demand states that, other things equal:
options: Higher prices lead to lower quantity demanded
Higher prices lead to higher quantity demanded
Price and demand are unrelated
Quantity demanded depends only on income

questions.question: Why must demand include both 'willing AND able' to buy?
options: Because wanting something without money to pay for it does not affect the market
Because sellers check buyers' bank accounts
Because willingness alone raises prices
Because ability alone is enough to create demand

questions.question: The price of maize meal itself rises and buyers purchase less. On the diagram this appears as:
options: A leftward shift of the whole demand curve
A movement along the same demand curve to a new point
A rightward shift of the demand curve
A shift of the supply curve

questions.question: Which event would shift the entire demand curve for maize meal to the RIGHT?
options: A fall in the price of maize meal
A rise in consumer income
A drought destroying the harvest
A fall in the price of bread, a substitute

questions.question: Why does the supply curve slope upward?
options: Because producers prefer selling less at high prices
Because a higher price rewards producers, making it worthwhile to offer more
Because buyers demand more at high prices
Because costs always fall as production rises

questions.question: The drought halves the maize harvest. Why does this SHIFT the supply curve instead of moving along it?
options: Because the change was caused by weather, not by the maize price
Because all changes shift the curve
Because demand changed at the same time
Because the harvest is measured in tons, not rands

questions.question: After the drought, the supply curve shifts:
options: Rightward — more offered at every price
Leftward — less offered at every price
It does not move; only demand moves
It becomes horizontal

questions.question: Which of these would shift the supply curve of maize meal RIGHTWARD?
options: A rise in fertiliser costs
A new tax on millers
Improved farming technology raising yields
A drought

questions.question: At the equilibrium price:
options: Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied and the market clears
There is always a small surplus
Sellers make maximum profit
Government sets the price officially

questions.question: If the market price sits ABOVE equilibrium, what happens?
options: A shortage forms and price rises further
A surplus forms — unsold stock pushes sellers to cut the price toward equilibrium
The demand curve shifts left
Nothing; any price can last forever

questions.question: A price below equilibrium creates:
options: A surplus, so price falls
Equilibrium immediately
A shortage — buyers bid the price up toward equilibrium
A shift of both curves

subtopics.title: The Drought Diagram — Working the Full Example

questions.question: In the drought example, why does the demand curve stay where it is?
options: Because demand curves never move
Because consumer income and other demand conditions are unchanged
Because the drought reduced demand too
Because price changes shift demand

questions.question: Comparing the new equilibrium to the old one after the supply shift, we find:
options: Higher price, smaller quantity traded
Lower price, larger quantity traded
Higher price, larger quantity traded
Both price and quantity unchanged

questions.question: At the OLD price, immediately after the drought shifts supply left, the market experiences:
options: A surplus of maize meal
A shortage — quantity demanded exceeds the reduced quantity supplied
Instant equilibrium
Falling prices

questions.question: As the maize price rises toward the new equilibrium, buyers reducing their purchases is shown as:
options: A leftward shift of the demand curve
A movement along the demand curve
A rightward shift of supply
A new demand curve being drawn
